# Chart Bar

```tsx
import { ChartBar } from "@s0l/design-system"
```

A stacked bar with its Legend. Mirrors the Figma Chart Bar: give it `items`, and each segment is as wide as its share of the values. The total row is always the sum of the items. With a `max` above that sum, the rest of the Track shows, as in Items=1. It takes 100% of the width of its container.

## Example

From the Storybook story; names like `args` or `label` are the story controls.

```tsx
renderChart(allArgs, itemCount)
```

## Figma notes

Mirrors the Figma Chart Bar: the Legend as a List, the Bars and, past one item, the total row (a Chart Legend Item with Color=None). Items are not variants here: they come from `items`, so any amount works, and the segments, the Legend and the total all follow the values.
Each segment is as wide as its share of the bar, left to right in the order of `items`: the width always follows the value. The Figma segments are all the same width only because the samples are. The total row always shows the sum of the items.
By default the items fill the bar. With a `max` above their sum, the rest of the Track shows, as in Items=1.
The width is 100% of the container.

## Props

Documented props only; every component also accepts the props of the element or Base UI part it renders (`className`, events, ARIA…).

`ChartBarProps`:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `ChartBarItem[]` | Figma Items. |
| `max?` | `number` | What a full bar stands for. By default, the sum of the items. Above it, the rest of the Track shows. It never changes the total row, which is the sum. |
| `totalLabel?` | `string` | The label of the total row. |
| `showTotal?` | `boolean` | The total row. By default, only past one item, as in Figma. |
| `valueType?` | `ChartBarValueType` | What the values are. As `percent`, 75 reads 75%. |
| `currency?` | `string` | The ISO code of the money, for `valueType="currency"`. |

## Types

`ChartBarItem`, `ChartBarProps`, `ChartBarValueType`

## Rules

- Import `ChartBar` from `@s0l/design-system`. Do not rebuild it with plain HTML and Tailwind classes.
- Style it through its props and variants first. Use `className` only for layout (margin, width, grid placement), never to change its colors, typography or radius.
- Colors come from the S0L tokens; see [color](../foundations/color.md).
